en: Mount Mayon in the Philippines is a classic stratovolcano known for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest volcano in the solar system, standing about 22 kilometers high.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of limestone, a sedimentary rock formed from ancient marine organisms.
The Tycho crater on the Moon features prominent ray systems made of bright material ejected during impact.
Baguio City experiences a cooler climate than Manila because its higher elevation lowers the average temperature.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines and plays a crucial role in the local water cycle.
Sirius, also known as the Dog Star, is the brightest star visible in the night sky from Earth.
The rich andosol soil around Mount Kanlaon in Negros Occidental is highly fertile due to volcanic ash.
Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter and is classified as a dwarf planet.
Typhoon Haiyan, locally named Yolanda, was one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded to make landfall.
The Philippine Trench is a deep oceanic trench formed by the subduction of the Philippine Sea plate.
A seismograph is the specific scientific instrument used to measure and record ground movements during an earthquake.
